item.title: Ba crowned BOG champions after 8 years, edging Rewa 2-1
item.description: Hosts Dayal’s Steel Ba have been crowned the Extra Battle of the Giants champions after 8 years, edging Stratum/PPCL Rewa 2-1 in the final at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba. Former Ba captain Praneel Naidu was among the scorers for the Men in Black, while Penisoni Tirau, a former Coca-Cola Games long jump gold medallist, also found the back of the net for Ba.
item.content:encoded:
Hosts Dayal’s Steel Ba have been crowned the Extra Battle of the Giants champions after 8 years, edging Stratum/PPCL Rewa 2-1 in the final at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba.

Former Ba captain Praneel Naidu was among the scorers for the Men in Black, while Penisoni Tirau, a former Coca-Cola Games long jump gold medallist, also found the back of the net for Ba.

Naidu was also named the Player of the Match.

Rewa fought back in the second half when substitute Merrill Nand scored to give the Delta side hope, despite being down to 10 players.

Ba has been awarded $17,000 in prize money.

This is Ba’s third major title of the year, following their Extra Premier League and BiC Fiji FACT victories.

The final whistle sparked wild celebrations among the Ba players and supporters, with the packed crowd erupting as the hosts were crowned champions.

A total of 9,769 people came out to witness the final.

All teams will now turn their focus to the Inter-District Championship.

item.title: Flying Fijians eye third straight Pacific Nations Cup title
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/09/2026 The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will be bidding for a third consecutive Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup title when they meet Japan in the final next Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/09/2026

The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will be bidding for a third consecutive Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup title when they meet Japan in the final next Saturday.

Fiji, who have won the title a record seven times, beat Canada 45-29, while the Brave Blossoms ran out 63-14 winners over the USA.

The two victorious semi-finalists will now meet in the title decider for the third successive year.

The match will also be an important one for interim head coach Senirusi Seruvakula, who is still searching for his first tournament win since taking over from Mick Byrne in April this year.

The Flying Fijians will meet Japan at 10.05pm next Saturday at Prince Chichibu Stadium in Tokyo.

item.title: Ryan Garcia stops Conor Benn in round two to retain WBC welterweight world title
item.description: Ryan Garcia picked up a crushing knockout victory of Conor Benn in Las Vegas, marking the first successful defense of Garcia's reign as WBC welterweight champion. As expected, Garcia was looking for his trademark left hook early in the fight, and he landed it several times in the opening moments.
item.content:encoded:
Ryan Garcia picked up a crushing knockout victory of Conor Benn in Las Vegas, marking the first successful defense of Garcia's reign as WBC welterweight champion.

As expected, Garcia was looking for his trademark left hook early in the fight, and he landed it several times in the opening moments.

Also as expected, Benn was willing to take punches and continue walking forward, trying to find a way to land his own big shots.

With the opening round fought at a fast pace, and both men using near-constant movement, it appeared fans would get an answer to how each fighter's weight cut would affect them as the rounds ticked by.

Then, Garcia decided there was no need to test anyone's gas tank.

A bomb of a right hand landed for Garcia in Round 2, dropping Benn to the canvas.

Benn managed to rise to his feet, but was still clearly compromised from the shot.

Garcia smelled blood in the water and unloaded his arsenal as Benn was trapped against the ropes.

With Benn no longer fighting back, the referee was forced to waive off the fight at the 1:25 mark of the second round.

After the win Garcia says he has always had a right hand, but he always had injuries, adding these are the first two fights with no injuries to his right hand.

After the fight, Garcia was quick to call out another young, brash and popular fighter in Teofimo Lopez.

In his most recent fight, Lopez won the WBA welterweight belt with a majority decision over Rolando "Rolly" Romero, who defeated Garcia in May 2025.

Garcia called Lopez to the ring, which led to Lopez and his entourage scuffling with ringside security before being held out of the ring.

item.title: South Africa claim Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry trophy as All Blacks fall short in final Test
item.description: The Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour has ended in heartbreak, with South Africa defeating the All Blacks 43-28 in a nail-biting fourth test. The Springboks lead the All Blacks 17-14 at halftime in Baltimore.
item.content:encoded:
The Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour has ended in heartbreak, with South Africa defeating the All Blacks 43-28 in a nail-biting fourth test.

The Springboks lead the All Blacks 17-14 at halftime in Baltimore.

They dominated for much of the first half, but the All Blacks struck back with four minutes left when Will Jordan surged over for a try, to go with one from Codie Taylor early in the game.

There was a lengthy delay midway through the first half, when referee Karl Dickson lost communication with the Television Match Official.

Play resumed after the two captains agreed that there would not be TMO involvement unless there was foul play, in which case a phone call would be made.

British Open golf winner Ryan Fox carred the New Zealand flag, standing next to the All Blacks at the pre-match anthem.

The All Blacks won the first Test 33-16, with the Springboks taking the next three games 33-26, 29-24 and now 43-28.

item.title: Rewa banking on fighting spirit in BOG final
item.description: Mansi Chand , Priya Nand · 13/09/2026 Stratum/PPCL Rewa will be banking on the team’s fighting spirit to give them the strength they need when they take on Dayal’s Steel Ba this afternoon in the final of the Extra Battle of the Giants Tournament in Ba.
item.content:encoded:
Mansi Chand , Priya Nand · 13/09/2026

Stratum/PPCL Rewa will be banking on the team’s fighting spirit to give them the strength they need when they take on Dayal’s Steel Ba this afternoon in the final of the Extra Battle of the Giants Tournament in Ba.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Assistant Coach Priyant Mannu says the players have continued to fight despite the challenges they have faced and will need the same determination when they take on Ba this afternoon in the final.

He says playing Ba is not a new scenario for the team, as they faced the host side in the pool stages last week and secured a convincing 3-0 victory.

Mannu says the final will come down to how well Rewa controls the game.

The Delta Tigers are nine-time BOG champions and are chasing their 10th title, having last lifted the trophy in 2020.

However, Ba will be looking to turn the tables after beating Rewa 1-0 in their final Extra Premier League match last month.

The Men in Black are the most successful team in BOG history, with 17 titles, and are chasing their first BOG crown since 2018.

Ba are also looking for their third major title this season after winning the BiC Fiji FACT and Extra Premier League.

The final will be played at 3pm at 4R Stadium in Govind Park, Ba.
